hook: A very short Keter file about something too large to contain at all. There are no tests and no interviews, only scale and the measures used to hide it. Read it with a map of the southern Atlantic in your head and let the numbers do the work.
whyItMatters: SCP-169 is a compact take on the kaiju idea, an entity whose main anomaly is simply its size. Since nothing can be built around it, the containment section turns into a plan for suppressing information, a very Foundation-like answer to an impossible problem. The article borrows the old sailors' name of Leviathan and grounds it in satellite imagery and seismic readings.
thingsToNotice:
The reveal is in the description: a remote archipelago that drifted three kilometres turns out to be rocky plates on the back of a living arthropod somewhere between 2,000 and 8,000 km long, probably asleep and "breathing" in tremors every three months. If it ever shifts its depth, the islands simply go under.

The procedures say almost nothing about the creature and nearly everything about secrecy: doctored satellite images, a garrison pulled out under a sea-level excuse, endangered birds as a reason to keep people away. The coldest line is about the US Navy ship that found it, sunk with its entire crew straight afterwards with Washington's consent.

The addendum ties the anomaly to an ultra-low-frequency sound that NOAA picked up off South America's south-west coast, which the Foundation takes to be the creature's head. That puts the head thousands of kilometres from the islands, and it turns public curiosity about the noise into something to be stopped by any means.
